solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Fable perhaps in English, quite bloodthirsty all round

indicators.note: one thing being in another means it sits inside it, so a letter goes into the middle
going all round something means wrapping it, so the outer words surround the inner letter

blocks.note: quite, as in all or completely
standard abbreviation for English
gory means full of bloodshed

explanation.surface: A fable written in English turns out to be surprisingly violent from start to finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quite bloodthirsty' reads as one adjective phrase, but each word gives its own piece, and together they wrap around the language abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A fable is one kind of allegory, a story carrying a hidden moral meaning; 'perhaps' flags the example.

clue.text: Whoever keeps it up for first year one can protect

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase for a noun: something that can protect

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means reading from bottom to top, so the letters run backwards

indicators.text: keeps it up for first year
indicators.note: keeping one thing in place of another, here instead of a letter, signals a swap of letters

blocks.note: whoever, meaning any person at all
taken as written
Y is the abbreviation for year; it is the letter replaced

explanation.surface: Someone who keeps going for a whole first year at something deserves credit.
explanation.walkthrough: In ANYBODY, the first Y is swapped for IT written upwards, giving AN-TI-BODY.
explanation.definitionFit: Antibodies are blood proteins that defend the body against infection, so one is a thing that protects.

clue.text: Reason watch is kept on private clubs

blocks.note: lo, an old word meaning look or behold
a GI is an American private soldier
C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs

explanation.surface: Someone explains why private members' clubs are kept under surveillance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Private clubs' reads as one phrase but splits into an American soldier and a card suit; lo is an old word for look, and in a down clue the first piece sits on top.
explanation.definitionFit: Logic and reason are near synonyms, both meaning sound thinking or rational argument.

clue.text: Do the done thing with WWI novel

indicators.note: to do something can mean to work it over or fix it up, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Advice to behave properly in the manner of a First World War story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The done thing' is an idiom for correct behaviour, which hides that it is just letters to rearrange; WWI is the American Civil War novel's misdirection, wrong war.
explanation.definitionFit: Margaret Mitchell's 1936 book about the American Civil War South is a famous long work of fiction.

clue.text: Regret theorem — or sentiment framing it

indicators.note: a frame holds a picture inside it, so the phrase before carries the solution within its letters

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word, the whole short word and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A mathematician wonders whether to regret a theorem or merely feel sentimental about it.
explanation.walkthrough: The dash and the abstract nouns make it read as a choice between ideas, but the letters simply run on across the words.
explanation.definitionFit: Remorse is deep regret or guilt felt for a wrong that someone has done.

clue.text: Not budging from saint-like lives

definitions.note: an adjectival phrase for the noun: a state of not budging

blocks.note: ST is the abbreviation for saint
as, meaning like or in the manner of
is, meaning exists or lives

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to move away from living a life of saintly virtue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saint-like' looks like a single hyphenated adjective, but it splits into the saint abbreviation and a separate word for like.
explanation.definitionFit: Stasis is a state of inactivity or equilibrium where nothing changes or moves.

clue.text: Approving remark, ie missing one bearing greater resemblance to the other?

indicators.note: something missing is absent, so a letter is dropped from the expanded phrase

blocks.note: ie is the Latin abbreviation id est, read out in English as that is
the Roman numeral for one, the letter that is dropped

blocks.clueFragment: bearing greater resemblance to the other
blocks.note: looking more similar to the thing mentioned

explanation.surface: A compliment comparing two things, where the one lacking something looks more like the other.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping the I from THAT IS gives the contraction THAT'S; the rest is a literal paraphrase of the phrase's comparative meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: People say this phrase to show approval when something improves to meet their expectations.

clue.text: Has moved parrot on in hurry

indicators.note: letters that have been moved are shifted out of their order

blocks.note: taken as written
the kea is a New Zealand parrot
in cricket the on side is also called the leg side

explanation.surface: Someone has hurriedly relocated a pet parrot.
explanation.walkthrough: On and leg are interchangeable in cricket, where the on side of the field is the leg side.
explanation.definitionFit: Shake a leg is an informal idiom urging someone to hurry up and get moving.

clue.text: Like sauna was — yet different?

indicators.note: something different has been changed, so the letters take a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone describes what the sauna was like, yet suspects it was not the usual experience.
explanation.walkthrough: The dash makes the two short words seem separate thoughts, but together they are the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A sauna is a hot steam room that makes people perspire heavily, so it is damp with perspiration.

clue.text: Key on ring beneath father’s painting

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece placed on another sits above it, so it is written first
being beneath something in a down clue means sitting lower, so this pair is written after the other piece

blocks.note: Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest's title
the Escape key on a computer keyboard
a ring is round like the letter O

explanation.surface: A father keeps his key on a ring tucked beneath a painting.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, a piece placed on another sits above it, and one beneath sits below, so the father's abbreviation comes first and the ring last.
explanation.definitionFit: A fresco is a type of mural applied to wet plaster on a wall or ceiling.

clue.text: Good blocks hammered into cross

indicators.note: something hammered is beaten out of shape, so its letters are knocked about and reordered
a thing that blocks a passage sits in its middle, so one piece lodges inside another

blocks.note: G is the abbreviation for good
taken as written

explanation.surface: A craftsman hammers good blocks into the shape of a cross.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Into' looks like a preposition but is the material rearranged to TION, which then takes G in its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: A tigon is the hybrid offspring of a male tiger and a lioness, an animal crossbreed.

clue.text: Spread disease briefly after month, and end of quarantine

indicators.note: said briefly means cut short, so the word loses its final letter
the end of a word is its last letter, so only that one is kept

blocks.note: MAR is the abbreviation for March
a malady is an illness
the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A disease spread quickly a month ago, and then quarantine ended.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spread' looks like a verb about disease, but it is the definition as a noun; MALADY cut short comes after the month.
explanation.definitionFit: Marmalade is a citrus preserve that people spread on toast at breakfast.

clue.text: To sponsor youngsters in care maybe not progressive?

blocks.note: to back is to support or sponsor
wards are children placed under the protection of a guardian or court

explanation.surface: Is it a regressive policy to sponsor children in care?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maybe' marks youngsters in care as one example of wards.
explanation.definitionFit: Backwards describes something behind the times or regressive, the opposite of forward-looking or advanced.

clue.text: Meant to shower after son

indicators.note: coming after something means following it, so the piece mentioned first is placed second

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for son
to pelt is to shower with blows or rain down heavily

explanation.surface: Someone was supposed to take a shower after their son had his.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Meant' looks like a past tense of intending, but here it means signified, as in 'that spelt trouble'.
explanation.definitionFit: To spell can mean to signify or indicate a result, as in a sign that spelt disaster.

clue.text: River boat enters to bring conscript across pond

indicators.note: to enter something is to go inside it, so one piece is placed within another

blocks.note: the Dee is a river in Britain
a raft is a simple flat boat

explanation.surface: A boat comes upriver to carry a soldier across a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Across pond' is crossword shorthand for American usage, the Atlantic being the pond; Americans speak of the draft where Britons say conscription.
explanation.definitionFit: In the United States, someone called up for compulsory military service is drafted, making them a conscripted soldier.

clue.text: Coming to an understanding within a faction

indicators.note: within means inside, so one piece is set inside another

blocks.note: a wing of a party is one faction of it
an, the indefinite article as a single letter
ken means knowledge or understanding

explanation.surface: Members of a faction finally reach agreement among themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coming to an understanding' reads as one idiom, but the definition is only 'Coming to', meaning regaining consciousness; A KEN sits inside A WING.
explanation.definitionFit: Coming to means regaining consciousness, waking up after fainting or sleep, which is what awakening describes.

clue.text: Got Google always to unearth golf player from Ireland

indicators.note: to unearth is to dig something out, and always means every time it occurs, so every copy is removed

blocks.note: taken as written
Golf is G in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone searched online to dig up details on an Irish golfer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Golf player' wants to be a golfer, but golf is the letter G and the player is an actor; Peter O'Toole was an Irish-born film star.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter O'Toole, star of Lawrence of Arabia, was an actor, and actors are players, born in Ireland.

clue.text: Typical of gown with fastener: opening but not right!

indicators.note: but not means excluding, so one letter is taken away

blocks.note: a stud is a small fastener on clothing
an entry is an opening or way in
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A dress-maker complains that a gown's fastener ruins the opening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Town and gown' contrasts locals with a university, so gown stands for the academic community; the gown and fastener make it seem about dressmaking.
explanation.definitionFit: Gown is a metonym for university members, so typical of them is characteristic of students.

clue.text: PC’s associate recoiling before chief

indicators.note: to recoil is to spring back, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: a pal is a friend or associate
top, meaning chief or leading

explanation.surface: A police constable's partner flinches in front of the chief officer.
explanation.walkthrough: PC wants to be a police constable, as the British use it; here it is a personal computer.
explanation.definitionFit: A laptop is a portable personal computer, the kind of machine abbreviated as a PC.

clue.text: The Speaker’s looked briefly annoyed

indicators.note: what a speaker produces is speech, so the word is identified by how it is pronounced

blocks.note: to peek is to take a quick look

explanation.surface: The Speaker of the House glanced up with irritation at the chamber.
explanation.walkthrough: The Speaker sounds like the parliamentary chair, but just marks a sound-alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Piqued means irritated or resentful, especially when someone's pride has been wounded.

clue.text: Disregard for commentator’s dexterity

indicators.note: a commentator talks over the air, so what matters is how the word is pronounced

blocks.note: to slight someone is to disregard them

explanation.surface: Someone shows contempt for a sports broadcaster's skill.
explanation.walkthrough: The word for an insult and the word for skill of hand are pronounced the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleight means skill or cunning with the hands, as in sleight of hand performed by conjurors.

clue.text: Old paramilitaries, each drinking pale port

indicators.note: someone drinking takes something in, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: the SS was the Nazi paramilitary force
wan means pale or pallid
EA is the abbreviation for each

explanation.surface: Old soldiers each down a glass of pale ale, or port wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pale port' looks like a drink, but pale is the inserted word and port the definition; SWANSEA is a port city in South Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Swansea is a coastal city in South Wales with a harbour and docks on the Bristol Channel.

clue.text: Accident has old lady keeping rather quiet

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it, so one piece holds another inside

blocks.note: an old lady is slang for one's mother, ma
-ish as a suffix or informal word means somewhat or rather
P is piano, the musical direction for quiet

explanation.surface: An elderly woman has had an accident and is keeping quiet about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rather quiet' reads as one phrase, but splits into two pieces, one inside the mother figure and one after.
explanation.definitionFit: A mishap is a minor accident or unlucky event, something going wrong by chance.

clue.text: Maybe miss seeing red and green snake finally

indicators.note: finally points to what comes at the end, so only the last letters are kept

blocks.note: seeing red means being angry, and ire is anger
the final letter of each of the two words

explanation.surface: Someone could miss the sight of a red and green snake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Miss' looks like a verb, but it is a young woman, and Irene is one possible name for her.
explanation.definitionFit: Irene is a girl's name, so a miss, an unmarried young woman, might be called that.

clue.text: Weakened through heat?

blocks.note: first meaning: toned down or limited, as a statement with reservations
second meaning: advanced from a preliminary race to the next round

explanation.walkthrough: 'Heat' suggests temperature softening something, but it is a qualifying round in a race.
explanation.definitionFit: A qualified remark is hedged with conditions, and an athlete who wins a heat goes into the final.

clue.text: One loudly interrupting sister for a joke

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break into the middle, so a letter goes inside

blocks.note: Roman numeral for one
a nun is a religious sister
F is forte, the musical direction for loudly

explanation.surface: Someone noisily butts in on a sister's conversation just to tease.
explanation.walkthrough: The sister is a nun, split by the musical letter for loud, with I placed in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something in fun means doing it playfully, as a jest rather than seriously.

clue.text: Ability to trigger alarm and any amount of locks?

blocks.note: first meaning: scariness, from the informal sense of hairy as frightening
second meaning: the state of having plenty of growth on the head

explanation.surface: A security system's ability to set off an alarm whenever any lock is tampered with.
explanation.walkthrough: Alarm and locks suggest a burglar alarm, but locks are tresses of growth on the head.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, a hairy moment is a frightening one, and the noun also literally describes having abundant locks.

clue.text: Having delicate appeal that’s shown to conclude Spanish film?

definitions.text: that’s shown to conclude Spanish film
definitions.note: a cryptic second definition: the closing caption of a Spanish film, two words

blocks.note: first meaning: small, dainty and charming, like a fairy

blocks.clueFragment: that’s shown to conclude Spanish film
blocks.note: second meaning: Spanish for 'the end', the caption at the close of a movie

explanation.surface: A charming screen ending that closes a Spanish movie.
explanation.walkthrough: Spanish films end with the caption 'el fin', the Spanish for 'the end', which runs together to make the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Elfin describes someone small, slender and delicately pretty, with the charm of a fairy creature.

clue.text: Make space for retreat at a temple

indicators.note: to retreat is to go back, so the letters run the other way

blocks.note: to do is to make
a gap is a space
taken as written

explanation.surface: Clear room for a religious retreat at a temple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retreat' seems to be a spiritual retreat, but it tells you to read the first two words' letters backwards before adding the article.
explanation.definitionFit: A pagoda is a tiered tower used as a Buddhist or Hindu temple in Asia.

clue.text: Fancy, but so devoid of reason

definitions.note: so turns the adjectival phrase into an adverb: in a way devoid of reason

blocks.note: to fancy something is to want it
but, as in only or merely

explanation.surface: Someone's whim is attractive but entirely irrational.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy' looks like an adjective meaning elaborate, but it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To act wantonly is to act without motive, provocation or justification, gratuitously and recklessly.
